title: Myth: a generator is enough backup for critical systems

scenes.headline: A generator is enough backup for critical systems.
scenes.voice: Many organisations believe a generator is all the backup their critical systems will ever need.

scenes.headline: Generators start late, need fuel, and fail unnoticed.
lines: Fuel must reach the site in time
A missed service shows up on the worst day
scenes.voice: In reality, a generator takes time to start, and sensitive equipment drops in that gap. It depends on fuel reaching the site, and a missed service only shows up on the worst possible day.

scenes.headline: Layer the backup.
scenes.voice: Critical loads need several layers of protection working together. A UPS for the first seconds, batteries for the hours, solar to recharge them, and the generator as the last layer.

scenes.headline: Request an executive briefing
